::: {.callout-important}
## Read this before you start

Every polynomial on this sheet is given **expanded**. None of them factorises usefully, and that is
deliberate: in the class material you could often read the roots straight off the brackets, so the
derivative method never had to do any work. Here it is the only route.

For every question, the same five steps:

1. Move the constant to the right, so the equation reads $g(x)=c$.
2. Fix the direction of the two ends from the leading term.
3. Solve $g'(x)=0$ — this is where the factorising happens, and it will come out.
4. Evaluate $g$ at each stationary point and compare with $c$: **above or below is all you need**.
5. Count one crossing for each monotone stretch whose two ends lie on opposite sides of $y=c$.
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Answer form.** Section A: a whole number. Section B and C: an inequality or a set of values of the
constant, written in interval form or as an inequality — and say explicitly whether each endpoint is
included. Section C question 11 asks for a letter.

**Total: 42 marks.**
:::

---

- [ ] I solved $g'(x)=0$ completely and checked I had found **all** the real stationary points.
- [ ] I compared each turning value with $c$ using "above or below", not the exact gap.
- [ ] I counted monotone stretches, not brackets.
- [ ] Where a stationary point was a point of inflection, I said so and did **not** count a stretch there.
- [ ] For Section B and C I checked each endpoint separately, and said whether it is included.
